mainTopic: Searching for a source that דברים שבלב אינן דברים (thoughts kept in the heart don't count): five attempted proofs; four are pushed off, and the מעילה proof stands
overview: The גמרא looks for a source for the rule דברים שבלב אינן דברים: a thought a person keeps in his heart, without saying it out loud, has no legal effect. The first four proofs are each pushed off. These are the forced קרבן, the forced גט or freeing of a slave, רב יוסף's mistaken groom, and אביי's woman who says she wanted the קידושין anyway. The fifth proof, רב חייא בר אבין's case of מעילה, is also pushed off at first: maybe the owner is lying to escape a קרבן. But the גמרא then shows he had an innocent excuse he did not use, so the proof stands. Next come two stories of men who sold their property planning to move to ארץ ישראל, with two versions each of what רבא and רב אשי ruled. Then new משניות begin. The first is about an agent who makes קידושין in a different place, with a parallel rule for a גט and an explanation of why both are needed. The second is about conditions concerning נדרים and מומין, with an explanation of why the same rule also appears in כתובות. The amud ends with the start of a משנה about קידושין with less than a שווה פרוטה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a man is forced to bring his קרבן, yet it must be 'by his will'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that we force a man to bring his קרבן עולה, but also that it must be 'according to his will.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He shall offer it' teaches that we force him. Could it mean even against his will? The פסוק says: 'according to his will.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that it will use as its first proof. This step only sets up the source; the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק seems to say two opposite things. 'He shall offer it' means we can force him to bring his קרבן. 'According to his will' means it has to be something he wants. The ברייתא will settle this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We force or pressure him (the בית דין does)

phrases.english: "He shall offer it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3

phrases.english: teaches that they force him.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a man who promised a קרבן and then didn't want to bring it.

phrases.english: I might think: even against his will?
The verse says: "according to his will."
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the first proof the גמרא brings for דברים שבלב אינן דברים.
steps.raayaObject: The rule דברים שבלב אינן דברים

steps.title: How both parts fit: force him until he says 'I want'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא fits the two parts of the פסוק together: we pressure him until he says 'I want.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How is that? We force him until he says: 'I want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own puzzle. We are allowed to pressure him, and once he says 'I want,' the קרבן counts as 'according to his will.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The force and the 'will' are not in conflict. Pressure is what leads him to say 'I want,' and the spoken words are what make it count as his will. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step: what about what he really feels inside?

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (a phrase used to fit two ideas together)

phrases.english: How so?
They force him until he says: "I want."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two opposite readings from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fitting two parts of a פסוק together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Force and 'his will' seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pressure is allowed until he says 'I want,' and then it counts as his will.

steps.title: The proof: his heart disagrees, yet his words count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why 'I want' works when he really doesn't want it, and suggests the reason is דברים שבלב אינן דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why does it work? In his heart he isn't happy with it! Isn't it because we say that thoughts in the heart are not legally meaningful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now draws its proof from the ברייתא. His spoken 'I want' counts even though his heart says 'no.' That suggests unspoken thoughts don't count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside, the man still doesn't want to bring the קרבן. If his inner feelings mattered, the קרבן would not be 'according to his will.' Since the ברייתא accepts it, it seems only the spoken words matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not pleased with it
Matters kept in the heart are not legally meaningful

phrases.english: But why?
But in his heart he is not pleased with it!
Rather, is it not because we say:
Matters in the heart are not matters?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי הָא בְּלִבֵּיהּ לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ruling in Step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His forced 'I want' works even though his heart disagrees.

steps.title: Rejected: deep down he does want the כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. We can be sure he truly wants the כפרה, so his heart really agrees with what he said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps that case is different, since we can testify that he wants to be forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first proof. In this case the man's heart is not really against his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who brings a קרבן gets כפרה, and every Jew deep down wants that. So when he says 'I want,' his heart agrees with him. This case does not show that thoughts against one's words are ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps there it is different
We are witnesses: it is obvious to everyone

phrases.english: But perhaps there it is different,
since we are witnesses
phrases.notes: He means: we can be sure of this without asking him.

phrases.english: that he is pleased with atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the רישא of the ברייתא (the קרבן case)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His true inner wish (to get כפרה) agrees with his words, so there is no conflict between heart and words.

steps.title: Second proof: a forced גט or forced freeing of a slave
steps.stepSummary: From the end of the ברייתא: a man forced to give a גט or free a slave is pressured until he says 'I want.' This again suggests דברים שבלב אינן דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from the end: similarly with divorce documents and slave-freeing documents, we force him until he says 'I want.' Why does that work, when in his heart he doesn't want it? Isn't it because thoughts in the heart don't count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again, using the second half of the same ברייתא. Here there is no כפרה to make him want it inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 4 worked only because of כפרה. A man forced to divorce his wife or free his slave gets no כפרה, so his heart really seems to be against it. Even so, his forced 'I want' works.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rather, from the latter clause:
And similarly you find with bills of divorce for women
and documents freeing slaves,
They force him until he says: "I want."

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי? הָא בְּלִבֵּיהּ לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: But why? In his heart he is not pleased with it!
Rather, is it not because we say
matters in the heart are not matters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof is rejected, the גמרא brings a new proof from the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא: a forced גט or forced freeing of a slave

steps.title: Rejected: deep down he wants to obey the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: This proof is also pushed off. It is a מצוה to listen to the חכמים, so deep down he wants to do what they ruled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps that case is different, because it is a מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof the same way it rejected the first. His heart may really agree with his words after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the חכמים have told him to give the גט, a Jew deep down wants to keep the מצוה of listening to them. So his 'I want' matches what he truly wants inside. Again, there is no real conflict between heart and words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים

phrases.english: But perhaps there it is different,
because it is a מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּמִצְוָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 5, using the same kind of answer as Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the סיפא (גט and freeing a slave)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His deeper wish to keep the מצוה of obeying the חכמים agrees with his words.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof: the man who was mistaken about his bride
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a case of a man who did קידושין with a mistaken idea in his mind. She is מקודשת anyway, which suggests his unspoken thought doesn't count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: prove it from here. A man did קידושין with a woman and then said: 'I thought she was a כהנת, and she is a לויה,' or 'a לויה, and she is a כהנת,' or 'poor, and she is rich,' or 'rich, and she is poor.' She is מקודשת, because she did not trick him. But why, when he says 'I thought'? Rather, it must be because thoughts in the heart don't count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a new proof from a case about קידושין. The man's mistaken idea was never said out loud, and the קידושין still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is stronger than the first two. Here we cannot claim his heart secretly agrees: he openly says he had something else in mind. Since she is מקודשת anyway, it seems an unspoken thought cannot cancel a deal.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does קידושין with a woman

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the קידושין works because he didn't care about the detail. He openly says he thought differently. The point is that a thought he never said out loud does not cancel the קידושין.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said: from here:
One who betroths a woman and said:
I thought that she was a priest's daughter
and she is a Levite's daughter,
or a Levite's daughter, and she turns out to be a priest's daughter,
or poor, and she is rich,
or rich, and she is poor:
she is betrothed, because she did not mislead him.
But why? He says: I thought otherwise!
phrases.notes: He only kept this idea in his head; he never made it a condition when he did the קידושין.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because we say
matters in the heart are not matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both proofs from the ברייתא fail, רב יוסף brings a new source from the laws of קידושין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a man who did קידושין while mistaken about the woman's family or wealth

steps.title: אביי rejects it: she is מקודשת only as a stringency
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that in that case the קידושין counts only לחומרא (as a stringency), so it does not prove his thoughts are ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: perhaps there it is different, because it is only a stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes off רב יוסף's proof. 'She is מקודשת' may only mean we treat her as married to be safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is treated as married only to be strict, she would need a גט before marrying someone else. That does not mean the קידושין is fully valid. So the case doesn't prove that his unspoken thought has no effect; it may only mean we are unsure and play it safe.

keyTerms.meaning: As a stringency: to be strict and safe, not as a final ruling

steps.whatToRemember: So far, all three proofs for דברים שבלב אינן דברים have been pushed off. The קרבן and גט cases fail because deep down he really agrees. The קידושין case fails because it may be only a stringency. More proofs follow in the next steps.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps there it is different, since it is a stringency.
phrases.notes: Literally 'for stringency.' He means she is treated as married only to be safe, so she would need a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דִּלְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's proof from the mistaken קידושין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'מקודשת' there may only mean married as a stringency, not fully married. So it shows nothing about whether thoughts in the heart are ignored.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the woman who says she wanted the betrothal anyway
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a proof from our משנה. A woman whose קידושין depended on a false condition says she wanted to marry him anyway, and she is still not מקודשת. That suggests her heart's thought does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said the proof is from here: in all these cases, even if she says 'In my heart I meant to become betrothed to him,' she is still not betrothed. Why not? She said it was in her heart!
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's proof was pushed off, אביי offers a new proof from the end of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the man said something like 'I am a כהן' and it turned out false, so the קידושין fails. Even when she says she wanted him anyway, she is not מקודשת. אביי reads this to mean her inner thought is ignored, which fits דברים שבלב אינן דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of them, meaning all the condition cases listed in the משנה
It was in my heart, meaning I privately intended it
From here, introducing a new source

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: from here:
In all of them, even though she said:
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the cases in our משנה where the man said something false about himself, like being a כהן.

phrases.english: "In my heart I meant to become betrothed to him"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: even so, she is not betrothed.
But why? She said "It was in my heart"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected proof with a new one from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that דברים שבלב אינן דברים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of our משנה: even if she says 'in my heart I wanted him,' she is not מקודשת.

steps.title: Her thought cannot cancel his spoken condition
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The man explicitly made a condition, and her private thought does not have the power to erase his condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there: since he made a condition, it is not in her power to uproot his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof by showing another reason the woman's thought doesn't help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that thoughts never count. The man said the condition out loud, and the קידושין depends on him too. She alone cannot cancel what he stated, so this case says nothing about thoughts in general.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in her power

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since he made a condition,
it is not in her power
to uproot his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's proof; the search for a source continues with the next proof in step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is decided by the man's spoken condition, which she cannot cancel. It is not about whether thoughts count.

steps.title: A real case decided from the agent who brought from the window
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין reports a case that came before רב חסדא and רב הונא, decided from a משנה in מעילה. An owner claims he privately meant a different place, but he is still guilty of מעילה. That suggests his thought is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חייא בר אבין said: there was a case in רב חסדא's study hall, and רב חסדא brought it to רב הונא's study hall, and they decided it from this: one who tells his agent 'Bring me from the window or from the box,' and the agent brings it. Even though the owner says 'I only meant this other one,' since the agent brought it from that place, the owner has committed מעילה. Why? He said 'in my heart'! Isn't it because we say thoughts in the heart are not legally meaningful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fresh proof, an actual case decided by great אמוראים from a משנה about מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent did what the owner said out loud, and the item turned out to be הקדש. The owner claims he privately meant another place, which would mean the agent didn't act for him. Since the owner is still guilty, the proof says his unspoken thought doesn't count.

keyTerms.meaning: He committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש property
Thoughts kept in the heart are not legally meaningful

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chiya bar Avin said:
There was an incident in Rav Chisda's study hall,
and Rav Chisda brought it to Rav Huna's study hall,
phrases.notes: The word "brought" isn't written. The גמרא assumes it.

phrases.english: and they resolved it from this:
phrases.notes: "This" is a משנה in מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: One who says to his agent:
"Bring me from the window ledge
or from the box," and he brought it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת:
phrases.english: Even though the owner said:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא הָיָה לִי בְּלִבִּי אֶלָּא עַל זֶה״,
phrases.english: "In my heart I meant only this one,"
since he brought it to him from that one,
the owner has committed misuse of consecrated property.
But why? He said "in my heart"!
Rather, is it not because we say
that matters in the heart are not matters?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין: עוֹבָדָא הֲוָה בֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since אביי's proof failed, a new proof is brought from מעילה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that דברים שבלב אינן דברים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעילה: the owner is guilty of מעילה even though he claims he privately meant a different place.

steps.title: Maybe he is just trying to escape a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. We don't believe the owner because he may be making up his claim to avoid bringing a קרבן for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there, because he is trying to exempt himself from a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the מעילה proof by saying the owner's claim is suspicious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His thought is not ignored because thoughts never count. It is ignored because we don't trust him: claiming 'I meant somewhere else' gets him out of a קרבן. So this case does not prove the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering, here the קרבן מעילה owed for accidental misuse

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since he is coming to exempt himself from an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּלְמִיפְטַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ מִקׇּרְבָּן קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The owner's claim may be a lie to escape a קרבן, so the case is about trustworthiness, not whether thoughts count.

steps.title: He could have just said he did it on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. If he only wanted to escape the קרבן, he could have claimed he sinned on purpose, since a מזיד brings no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could have said it was on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection in step 12, saying the owner had an easier way out if he were lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן for מעילה is brought only for an accidental sin, not a deliberate one. If the owner were lying to escape the קרבן, he would just say 'I did it on purpose.' Since he chose a different claim, maybe he is telling the truth, and the proof comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, deliberately, which brings no קרבן
He should have said, or he could have said

phrases.english: He could have said
"It was on purpose"!
phrases.notes: Someone who misuses הקדש on purpose doesn't bring a קרבן, so this would also have gotten him out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner is lying to escape a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A liar would pick the simplest exemption, saying he sinned on purpose. Since he didn't, his claim seems honest.

steps.title: No one wants to call himself wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person does not like to label himself a רשע. So he picks the excuse that keeps him innocent, and the suspicion of lying stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person does not make himself out to be wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection in step 12, explaining why the owner wouldn't claim he sinned on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I did it on purpose' would get him out of the קרבן but make him look like a רשע. People avoid that, so he chose 'I meant a different place' instead. His claim is still suspicious, so the מעילה case still does not prove דברים שבלב אינן דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not do, meaning people don't normally act this way

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof is pushed off because she cannot cancel his spoken condition. The מעילה proof is now under attack: the owner may be lying to escape a קרבן, and he wouldn't call himself a רשע. The next step answers this and brings the מעילה proof back.

phrases.english: A person does not act
to make himself a wicked person.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ דִּמְשַׁוֵּי נַפְשֵׁיהּ רַשִּׁיעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and keeps the rejection of step 12 standing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he were lying, he would just say he sinned on purpose, so his claim must be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: People avoid labeling themselves a רשע, so he would choose a different excuse. For now the suspicion remains and the proof from מעילה seems to fail, but step 15 challenges this and brings the proof back.

steps.title: He could have claimed 'I remembered'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 14. The owner had an excuse that kept him innocent and also freed him from the קרבן, so he probably was not lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could have said "I remembered," as we learned in a משנה: if the owner remembered and the agent did not remember, the agent is guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer that the owner is probably lying to escape the קרבן. He had a better excuse that he did not use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said a person won't call himself a רשע, so he picks an innocent excuse. But "I remembered it was הקדש after I sent the agent" is also innocent, and it would make the agent liable instead of him. Since he didn't say that, he is likely honest, and the proof that private thoughts don't count comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (here, the one who sent the agent)
Is guilty of misusing הקדש property

steps.whyThisMatters: No answer is given, so the proof from מעילה stands. A private intention that was never spoken is ignored even when the person is believed.

phrases.english: He should have said: "I remembered,"
phrases.notes: He means: after sending the agent, I remembered the item was הקדש.

phrases.english: as we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה in מעילה from step 11.

phrases.english: If the owner remembered,
and the agent did not remember,
the agent is guilty of מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14 and brings back the proof of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner chose a lying excuse that keeps him innocent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An excuse that is both innocent and exempt was available. Not using it shows he was not inventing a story to escape the קרבן.

steps.title: Sold to move to ארץ ישראל but could not settle
steps.stepSummary: A man sold his property planning to go up to ארץ ישראל. He went but could not settle there. רבא rules that the sale can be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sold his property with the intention of going up to ארץ ישראל. He went up but could not settle there. רבא said: anyone who goes up does so to live there, and this man could not settle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about a sale made because of a plan to move. רבא decides whether that plan affects the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's plan was "to go up," but רבא says the real meaning of going up is going up to live there. Since he could not live there, the purpose of the sale failed, so the sale can be canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: Was able to settle / live there

phrases.english: A certain man who sold his property
with the intention of going up to the Land of Israel.
He went up but was not able to settle there.
רבא said:
Anyone who goes up does so with the intention of living there,
and this man was not able to settle.
phrases.notes: So the purpose of the sale failed, and he can cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבְּנִינְהוּ לְנִיכְסֵיהּ אַדַּעְתָּא לְמִיסַּק לְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about how a person's intention affects a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going up means going up to settle. If he could not settle, the sale is undone.

steps.title: Second version: he went, so the sale stands
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבא's ruling says the plan was only to go up. He did go, so the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: his intention was to go up, and he did go up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's ruling, which reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the plan is read narrowly as just "going up," not "settling." Since that plan was fulfilled, the condition behind the sale was met and the sale cannot be canceled.

phrases.english: Some say:
It was with the intention of going up,
and he did go up.
phrases.notes: So the sale stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposite version of רבא's ruling in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The intention was only to go up. He went, so the sale is valid.

steps.title: Sold to move but never went
steps.stepSummary: A man sold his property planning to go up to ארץ ישראל but never went. רב אשי says he could have gone if he wanted, so the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sold his property with the intention of going up to ארץ ישראל. In the end he did not go up. רב אשי said: if he wanted, he could go up.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story: this time the man never went at all. רב אשי rules on whether he can cancel the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going was fully in his own hands. A buyer should not lose the sale just because the seller chose not to go, so the sale is valid.

phrases.english: A certain man who sold his property
with the intention of going up to the Land of Israel,
in the end did not go up.
רב אשי said:
If he wanted, he could go up.
phrases.notes: It was up to him, so the sale stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף לָא סְלֵיק. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי בָּעֵי, סָלֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A similar sale story, but here the man never went.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since he could have gone, the sale is not canceled.

steps.title: Second version: said as a question
steps.stepSummary: Another version has רב אשי asking: if he wanted, couldn't he have gone up?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: if he wanted, could he not have gone up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב אשי's words, said as a question instead of a statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a question, the words suggest the sale stands only because nothing actually stopped him. That opens the possibility that if something did stop him, the ruling would be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Could he not go up? (read as a question)

steps.confusionAlert: The words look almost the same as step 18. The difference is the tone: here it is a question, and that changes what it implies.

phrases.english: Some say:
If he wanted, could he not have gone up?
phrases.notes: Read this as a question. It hints that he really could have gone, and nothing stopped him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אִי בָּעֵי, לָא סָלֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב אשי's ruling, worded as a question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sale stands because nothing actually prevented him from going.

steps.title: What is the difference between the versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of רב אשי's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both versions say the sale stands here, so the גמרא asks when they would disagree. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story itself, both versions lead to the same result. The גמרא wants a case where the two wordings would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two versions in steps 18 and 19 differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two versions of רב אשי's words would give different rulings

steps.title: The difference: something stopped him on the way
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ when something beyond his control happened on the way and stopped him from going.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when something beyond his control happened on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions disagree when the man was stopped by forces outside his control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first version ("he could go if he wanted"), the sale stands anyway. By the question version, the sale stood only because nothing stopped him, so if he really was stopped, the sale is canceled.
steps.whatToRemember: When a sale is made for a known purpose, the outcome can depend on whether the purpose failed and whether he was forced. רבא and רב אשי each have two versions.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where something beyond his control came up on the way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If he was stopped by forces beyond his control: by the first version the sale stands, and by the question version it is canceled.

steps.title: משנה: Agent makes קידושין in a different place
steps.stepSummary: If a man tells his agent to make קידושין with a woman in a certain place, and the agent does it elsewhere, she is not מקודשת. If he only said where she is, she is מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who says to his agent, "Go and make קידושין for me with this woman in this place," and the agent went and made קידושין elsewhere, she is not מקודשת. If he said, "She is in this place," and the agent made קידושין elsewhere, she is מקודשת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about an agent who did not follow the place mentioned by the sender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place was part of the instruction ("make קידושין there"), the agent who changed it went beyond his mission, so the קידושין fail. If the place was only information ("she is there"), it was not a condition, so the קידושין work anywhere.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases mention a place. The difference is whether it was an order ("do it there") or only a description ("she is there").

phrases.english: משנה:
One who says to his agent:
"Go and make קידושין for me with so-and-so
in such-and-such a place,"
and he went and made קידושין with her in a different place,
she is not betrothed.
"She is in such-and-such a place,"
phrases.notes: Here the sender is just telling the agent where to find her.

phrases.english: and he made קידושין with her in a different place,
she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לִשְׁלוּחוֹ: ״צֵא וְקַדֵּשׁ לִי אִשָּׁה פְּלוֹנִית בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about an agent who departs from his instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A place given as an instruction binds the agent. A place given only as information does not.

steps.title: The same rule appears for a bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a משנה in גיטין teaches the same rule for a גט: if the husband said 'give it in place X', a different place makes it invalid. If he only said 'she is in place X', it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We also learned about divorce: If a man says 'Give this גט to my wife in such-and-such a place' and they gave it to her somewhere else, it is invalid. If he said 'She is in such-and-such a place' and they gave it somewhere else, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel משנה about a גט that matches our משנה about קידושין. This is setting up the next step, where the גמרא will ask why we need both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as in step 22. 'Give it in place X' is a real instruction, so changing the place breaks the שליחות. 'She is in place X' is just information, so the place does not matter. Because the two rules look identical, the next step has to explain why both are taught.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
And we also learned (in a משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And we also learned regarding bills of divorce:
One who says: 'Give this bill of divorce to my wife
in such-and-such a place,'
and they gave it to her in another place, it is invalid.
[If he said:] 'She is in such-and-such a place,'
and they gave it to her in another place, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel משנה about גט with the same rule as the קידושין משנה in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given in a different place from the one the husband named is invalid. If he only said where she is, it is valid.

steps.title: Why the divorce case is needed beyond betrothal
steps.stepSummary: Both teachings are needed. From קידושין alone we might think he only cares about the place because he wants a friendly crowd. In גירושין, where he is pushing her away, we might think he does not care.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to teach both. If we had only learned about קידושין, we would say he cares about the place because he is bringing her close: 'Here they love me and won't speak badly of me; there they hate me and will speak badly of me.' But by divorce, where he is pushing her away, you would say he doesn't care.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we need the divorce rule even though we already have the betrothal rule. Without it, we might think a husband does not care where a divorce happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידושין he has a clear reason to care about the place: he does not want to start his marriage where people dislike him and will gossip. In a divorce he is ending the relationship, so we might assume the place no longer matters to him. The גיטין משנה teaches that his instruction about the place still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to teach both cases)

phrases.english: And it is necessary [to teach both].
For if he had taught us only regarding betrothal,
[it would be] because he is coming to bring her close,
[thinking:] in this place they love me
and will not say things about me,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected spelling. The word means 'they speak.'

phrases.english: in that place they hate me
and will say things about me.
But regarding bills of divorce,
where he is coming to push her away,
say he does not care [about the place].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why both the קידושין and גיטין rules are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From קידושין alone, we might think a man does not care where a divorce happens.
steps.terutzMaskana: His instruction about the place matters in גירושין too.

steps.title: Why the betrothal case is needed beyond divorce
steps.stepSummary: From גירושין alone, we might think he only cares about the place because of the shame of divorce. In קידושין, which has no shame, we might think he does not care. So both are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only learned about divorce, we would say: in this place he is fine with being shamed, and in that place he is not. But by קידושין you would say he doesn't care. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning from the other side, explaining why the betrothal rule is needed too. It concludes that both teachings are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorce can be embarrassing, so a man might reasonably choose where he is willing to face that shame. קידושין has no embarrassment, so we might have assumed the place does not matter to him. Each case has its own reason, so neither can be learned from the other.
steps.whatToRemember: An instruction about the place counts in both קידושין and גירושין. Each case needs its own teaching because the man's reason for caring is different in each.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only regarding divorce,
[I would say:] in this place he is fine with being shamed,
in that place he is not fine with it,
but regarding betrothal,
say he does not care,
[therefore] it is necessary [to teach both].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of step 24 from the other direction and closes with צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the קידושין rule and the גיטין rule are needed, because each has its own reason why the man would care about the place.

steps.title: Betrothal on condition that she has no vows
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a man makes קידושין on condition that she has no נדרים and she does, she is not מקודשת. If he married her with no condition and she turns out to have נדרים, he may divorce her without paying the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man betroths a woman on condition that she has no vows, and vows are found on her, she is not betrothed. If he married her without saying anything, and vows are found on her, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a woman who has נדרים. It gives two cases: one where the man set a condition, and one where he said nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he set an explicit תנאי, the קידושין simply fails because the condition was not met. When he set no condition, the marriage stands. But since we assume he would not want a wife bound by vows, she loses her כתובה if he divorces her.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her without stating any condition
She leaves without her כתובה payment

steps.confusionAlert: In the second case the marriage itself works. The only result is that if they divorce, she does not get her כתובה money.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who betroths a woman
on condition that there are no vows upon her,
and vows were found upon her,
she is not betrothed.
If he married her without specifying,
and vows were found upon her,
she leaves without a marriage contract.
phrases.notes: He may divorce her, and she does not collect her כתובה money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין עָלֶיהָ נְדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: conditions about the woman's vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With an explicit condition of no vows, the קידושין fails if she has vows. Without a condition, the marriage stands, but she may be divorced without her כתובה.

steps.title: A condition that she has no blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same pattern as נדרים to מומין. A condition that fails means no קידושין. With no condition, he can divorce her without a כתובה. The blemishes that count are the ones that disqualify כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made קידושין on condition that she has no blemishes, and she does have blemishes, she is not מקודשת. If he married her with no condition and blemishes were found, she may be divorced without a כתובה. All the blemishes that disqualify כהנים also count for women.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from Step 26 continues. It now gives the same two rules for physical blemishes (מומין) that it gave for נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. In the first, he made an explicit condition, so the קידושין is void. In the second, he made no condition, so the marriage stands, but he was misled and does not have to pay the כתובה. The משנה then defines which blemishes count by pointing to the list for כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her with no condition stated
She leaves the marriage without receiving the כתובה payment
Those that disqualify כהנים from serving

steps.confusionAlert: In the second case she IS married. She still needs a גט. She just does not get her כתובה money.

phrases.english: On condition that she has no blemishes
and blemishes were found on her, she is not betrothed.
If he married her without any condition
and blemishes were found on her,
she leaves without a כתובה.
For all the blemishes that disqualify priests
also disqualify women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from נדרים to מומין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A failed condition about blemishes voids the קידושין. Unspecified blemishes allow divorce without a כתובה. The blemishes of כהנים are the standard.

steps.title: Why repeat what the משנה in כתובות already says?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a משנה in מסכת כתובות teaches this exact same rule. So why is it repeated here?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we already learned a משנה just like this about כתובות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה as repetitive, because the same teaching already appears in מסכת כתובות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to repeat a teaching for no reason. Since the rule about נדרים and מומין appears word for word in כתובות, the גמרא wants to know what this second copy adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And we also learned (in a משנה)

phrases.english: Gemara:
And we also learned
regarding כתובות
phrases.notes: He means the משנה in מסכת כתובות that teaches this same rule.

phrases.english: exactly like this!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי כְתוּבּוֹת כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה just quoted needs to appear in two places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same teaching already appears in כתובות, so this one seems repetitive.

steps.title: Each משנה needed only its own half
steps.stepSummary: Here the main point is the קידושין half, and the כתובה half came along with it. In כתובות the main point is the כתובה half, and the קידושין half came along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the תנא needed the rule about קידושין, and he taught the כתובות rule along with it. There, he needed the rule about כתובות, and he taught the קידושין rule along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the repetition is fine. Each מסכת needed a different half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מסכת קידושין, the new point is the first half: a failed condition cancels the קידושין. The second half was added only to complete the picture. In מסכת כתובות it is the reverse: the needed point is losing the כתובה, and the קידושין part was added to complete it.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed it (it was necessary to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: A משנה may repeat a teaching found elsewhere when each place needs a different part of it. The rest is taught only to complete the picture.

phrases.english: Here, he needed to teach about קידושין
phrases.notes: Here means our מסכת קידושין, and there means מסכת כתובות.

phrases.english: and he taught כתובות along with קידושין;
there, he needed to teach about כתובות
and he taught קידושין along with כתובות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each place has a different main focus; the extra half is added only to complete the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות are one teaching needlessly repeated
steps.terutzMaskana: Each משנה has its own needed half, so neither is redundant
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה teaches the קידושין rule. The משנה in כתובות teaches the כתובה rule.

steps.title: New משנה: קידושין with too little value, followed by gifts
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A man makes קידושין with two women using one פרוטה, or with one woman using less than a פרוטה, and later sends gifts. The ruling comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man makes קידושין with two women using one פרוטה's worth, or with one woman using less than a פרוטה's worth, even though he later sent gifts...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up the case, and the ruling will come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases each woman received less than a שווה פרוטה, which is the minimum for קידושין. The new detail is that he later sent the usual groom's gifts. The question being set up is whether those gifts show the קידושין took effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount for קידושין
Gifts a groom sends to his bride

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Wait for the ruling before deciding whether she is מקודשת.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who makes קידושין with two women with a פרוטה's worth
phrases.notes: Split between two women, each one gets less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: or with one woman
with less than a פרוטה's worth,
even though he sent gifts
afterward

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of קידושין with less than a שווה פרוטה, followed by gifts. The ruling comes next.
